item.title: Precincts, Not Posts
item.description: Over the past five years, American politics has celebrated a new archetype: the Gen Z candidate. They are fluent in both digital culture and political language and are often presented as the generation poised to rescue democracy from inertia. Yet beneath the rhetoric of renewal lies a more complicated reality. What does it actually take to run for congressional office […] The post Precincts, Not Posts appeared first on Brown Political Review.

item.title: Big Brother(s) Are Watching
item.description: George Orwell’s canonical work, 1984, warns of a future in which the all-powerful ‘Big Brother’ dictates truth by rewriting history so that only one version of the world can exist. item.title: License to Learn
item.description: Last year, Elon Musk proclaimed that AI was already smarter than the smartest person in the world, and soon will be smarter than all of the smartest people in the world collectively. No matter how one might feel about this statement, it is undeniable that AI has become deeply embedded in our daily routine. item.title: Fighting Absurdity with Absurdity: An Interview with Rob Potylo
item.description: Rob Potylo is a Massachusetts-born musical comedian and producer best known for his fictional alter ego, Robby Roadsteamer. After years in New England’s underground comedy, music, and radio scenes, Potylo recently gained national attention for performing parody songs at political hotspots across the country. item.title: The Melting Pot – Episode 2: Tea in Sahara
item.description: In The Melting Pot, Leyad Zavriyev ’27 explores the immigrant-run culinary scene of Rhode Island by interviewing local restaurant owners. This second episode features Mohamed, whose Moroccan café Tea in Sahara has been a beloved staple of the Providence community for over 15 years. item.title: Spray-Painting Politics: From Bed-Stuy to La Boca
item.description: In this photo collection, Leyad Zavriyev explores street art and graffiti from neighborhoods across the world – from Buenos Aires and San Juan, to Marrakech and Brooklyn. These walls tell stories of struggle, resilience, memory, and pride: remembering victims of dictatorship, honoring cultural icons, and calling for justice. item.title: The Inequality of Air Quality in America
item.description: Safe air is disproportionately concentrated in more affluent communities, while minorities and low income populations are burdened with higher pollution levels. The post The Inequality of Air Quality in America appeared first on Brown Political Review.
